subject: Elevator pitch: interop effort vs pricing — KiteBridge
messages:
From: Hector Ruiz <hector@kitebridge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Elevator pitch: interop effort vs pricing — KiteBridge

Grace —

Quick note from procurement: we received a packaged offer from AuroraAI (their hosted inference + migration assistance) that effectively lands 30% below your current list for comparable throughput. They included an onboarding credit and a 30-day pilot.

Before I share the full RFP, wanted to ask two things quickly:
1) Can Redwood match the headline price at parity if we accept a staged roll-out?
2) What is the realistic engineering/onboarding effort we should expect on our side (integration points: tokenization, KV cache warm-up, and model rollouts are our main risks)?

We have a procurement window that closes the week of Sep 7th. If you can put a concise counter or a pilot package together this week, that would be helpful.

Attached: kitebridge_rfp.pdf (summary).

Best,
Hector
Head of Platform Ops, KiteBridge
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Hector Ruiz <hector@kitebridge.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Elevator pitch: interop effort vs pricing — KiteBridge

Looping you both in — Hector just sent over an RFP summary. He says AuroraAI offered ~30% lower on price and included onboarding credit + 30-day pilot. Procurement window closes Sep 7.

Ask:
- Connor: can you give a ballpark of the engineering effort / risks on KB's side for onboarding (they mentioned tokenization differences and KV cache warm-up concerns). Also note whether Dedicated vs Hosted affects migration lift.
- Jordan: commercial options — what structured discount or pilot credit can we offer quickly without needing Exec sign-off? If we need a small exception we should surface it now.

I want a short 1-paragraph counter we can send Hector today. Keep it factual and focused on time-to-value, predictable latency, and lower long-term unit cost via our caching/batching.

Thanks —
Grace
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Hector Ruiz <hector@kitebridge.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Elevator pitch: interop effort vs pricing — KiteBridge

Grace — quick technical readout below. Attaching a short onboarding_estimate.xlsx with line items.

Summary (ballpark):
- Integration scope: tokenization parity check, KV cache warm-up strategy, routing fallbacks for model variants, and minor infra tweaks for prefix caching.
- Effort (KB engineering + Redwood support): approximately 2–3 full-time-weeks of joint work for a basic pilot (hosted API path). If they want Dedicated capacity + performance tuning, add 2 more weeks (mostly infra & validation).
- Risks: tokenization mismatch is the highest friction point; can be mitigated with a quick tokenization shim and a small set of canonical prompts (2–3 days to validate). KV cache warm-up is operational — we can provide a pre-warm runbook and an automated prefix cache script.
- Recommended minimal pilot: 30 days, hosted inference, 100K tokens/day baseline, include pre-warm runbook and a small onboarding service window (2 engineer-days from Redwood).

I'll also prepare a short bulleted tech blurb Grace can include in the counter (one-liner about predictable latency and minimal dev lift).

—Connor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Hector Ruiz <hector@kitebridge.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Elevator pitch: interop effort vs pricing — KiteBridge

Grace / team — commercial options we can move on fast without a long approval:

Option A (pilot-first — fast):
- 30-day pilot credit: $30,000 applied as usage credit on Hosted API (covers onboarding assistance & early traffic).
- No long-term commit required; if they convert within 60 days post-pilot we convert credit to a 3-month ramp discount.

Option B (staged parity):
- 10% upfront rebate for 6 months if they sign a 12-month consumption commitment (we protect margin via tiered commit levels).
- Include 2 proactive onboarding engineer-days and our pre-warm runbook.

Notes: anything deeper than Option A will likely need commercial leadership sign-off. If they insist on a 30% list cut we should request a realistic migration clause (e.g., 60-day conversion guarantee plus a three-month staged rate).

Suggested 1-line pitch for Hector to present to procurement: "We’ll stand up a 30-day pilot (no commit) with a $30k onboarding credit and a documented, low-friction migration runbook — ensuring predictable latency and no hidden egress penalties."

Jordan
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
From: Hector Ruiz <hector@kitebridge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 07:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Elevator pitch: interop effort vs pricing — KiteBridge

Thanks for the fast turnaround — this is helpful. Procurement likes the pilot approach; two clarifying asks:
1) Will the $30k credit be applied to Hosted usage only or can it be used against a Dedicated onboarding invoice if we choose that path?
2) Can you put the one-line pitch and the minimal tech assumptions (tokenization shim + pre-warm runbook) into a short PDF we can include in the RFP addendum?

If you can confirm those two items today we can present to procurement tomorrow and likely lock a decision before Sep 7.

Hector
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Hector Ruiz <hector@kitebridge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Elevator pitch: interop effort vs pricing — KiteBridge

Hector — confirmed and sending a tight proposal now. Quick answers:
1) The $30k pilot credit applies to Hosted API usage by default; we can make it fungible toward a one-time Dedicated onboarding invoice up to the same amount if KiteBridge elects Dedicated within 30 days of pilot completion (we’ll document that in the addendum).
2) Attached are the pilot-term-sheet.pdf and a 1-page tech blurb summarizing the tokenization shim, pre-warm runbook, and expected joint engineering days.

One-line pitch you can include in the RFP addendum: "Redwood will run a 30-day zero-commit pilot with a $30k onboarding credit and a documented migration runbook to ensure parity in latency and predictable unit costs during ramp."

Next steps: Hector — if procurement greenlights we’ll send a short DocuSign for the pilot terms and schedule an onboarding kickoff (Connor will lead the tech session). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-8642

Grace
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
